subject: Bug: Mean estimation in MGCFA differs in reordered dataset

messages.author: 4fe26caaac11aa72
messages.subject: Bug: Mean estimation in MGCFA differs in reordered dataset
parts:
Dear Yves, dear co-contributors to the superb lavaan-package,

I encountered a serious problem. Since I've checked the syntax several times, I fear it's a bug.

I'm estimating a three dim. model in a MGCFA context (i.e., strong measurement invariance) to compare means across sex groups. I wanted to bootstrap some parameters and wrote a short script that replicate the models. As a kind of syntax-check I tested the syntax without replacement (even though bootstrapping is actually with replacement), that is, the dataset is only reordered or shuffled.

By chance, I included besides Chi^2, CFI, and RMSEA, the mean difference (i.e., mean estimate of the second group). I got the following output:
        f1.diff       f2.diff       f3.diff        Chi         CFI        RMSEA
1     0.1839576    0.05487358    0.04239794   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
2    -0.1751234   -0.05654662   -0.03448976   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
3    -0.1751234   -0.05654662   -0.03448976   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
4     0.1839576    0.05487358    0.04239794   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
5    -0.1751234   -0.05654662   -0.03448976   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
6    -0.1751234   -0.05654662   -0.03448976   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
7     0.1839576    0.05487358    0.04239794   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
8    -0.1751234   -0.05654662   -0.03448976   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
9    -0.1751234   -0.05654662   -0.03448976   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722
10    0.1839576    0.05487358    0.04239794   309.7585   0.9810956   0.01670722

All the fit values are identical across the replication. However, the means differ (flip of the sign and some small changes in the values).
What I found out, is that it depends, on the group membership of the first case in the dataset. If it's a 2 you get the positive results, if it's a 1 you get the negative ones.
It does neither depend on the standardization of the latent variable nor the parameterization (delta vs. theta). Please also note, that the model converged normally.
I attached the reorder-model-estimation-syntax and a reduced data file.

Can someone tell me how to estimate the correct values?
What are the correct results?
How can I avoid different results?

Thanks in advance, kind regards.
Ulrich

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Bug: Mean estimation in MGCFA differs in reordered dataset
parts:
Dear Ulrich,

The groups labeled "1" and "2" are not necessarily sexes 1 and 2 in your data set.  Read about the "group.label" argument in the ?lavaan help page.  When the first group is sex "2" instead of sex "1", that affects which group's latent-response scales/residual variances are fixed vs. estimated (given that the loadings and thresholds are constrained to equality), as well as the sign of the latent mean-differences.  You will get consistent results when you use this argument:  fit.3dim <- cfa(..., group.label = c("1","2"), ...)

I noticed in your script you were saving the standardized means in group 2.  Like you, I would also expect them to be the same (with opposite sign) if all that changes is which sex is called "group 1", especially given that the fit measures match to so many decimal places.  But things get complicated with binary data.  A change in observed cell counts can be modeled equivalently either as a change in thresholds or a change in variance of the latent item-response, so I'm not sure whether the optimizer simply settles in a slightly different local maximum that happens to yield the same log-likelihood.  If you look at the output of lavInspect(fit.3dim, "cov.ov") when using sex 1 as either the first or second group, you will notice the model-implied polychoric correlations are the same, but the output of lavInspect(fit.3dim, "mean.ov") do not merely change signs in the second group's model-implied means (first group is a zero vector).  But there is no bug in how the standardized values are calculated.  If you calculate the standardized latent mean difference from the parameterEstimates() output (group 2 mean divided by the square-root of group 2 variance), you get what you see in the standardizeSolution() output. 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
